contract.major: Built for Meows contract {0}, but this shell provides {1}. Major versions must match.
contract.newer: Built for Meows contract {0}, which is newer than this shell's {1}. Update Meows, or rebuild the plugin against {1}.
contract.ui.major: Built against Avalonia {0}, but this shell hosts {1}. The two share one copy of Avalonia, so the major version has to match or the controls it builds are not controls this can show.
contract.ui.newer: Built against Avalonia {0}, which is newer than the {1} this shell provides. Update Meows, or rebuild the plugin against Avalonia {1}.
do.none: No plugin here has a job to run with no window.
do.off: {0} is switched off. Switch it on in Meows first; off means off, whoever asks.
do.unknown: There is no job called {0}. Meows.exe --do with nothing after it lists them.
history.compact.failed: Could not compact the file. Is it open elsewhere?
history.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Kibble writes a line when it sends a file, Purrge when it recycles one, Scruff when it posts, Portion when it shrinks. It all lands here, and it survives the window closing.
history.forget.done: Forgot {0} lines. The file is {1} now.
history.forget.prompt: Forget {0} lines older than {1}, from {2}? What was done before then is gone from here for good; the files themselves are not touched.
history.forget.prompt.all: Forget all {0} lines from {1}? They are gone from here for good; the files themselves are not touched.
history.title: What the plugins did
home.plugins.none: Nothing is switched on. The Plugins tab is next door.
home.title: Home
instinct.name: Instinct
instinct.outcome.notarget: {0} says it can do this but its tab does not answer. Tell whoever wrote it.
instinct.outcome.patience: Still going after {0} minutes, so Meows stopped waiting and called it off.
instinct.paused.runaway: Paused: it fired {0} times in {1} minutes, which is more than anyone usually means. Resume it if that was right.
instinct.state.noaction: {0} no longer offers “{1}”. The rule stays here in case a later version does.
instinct.state.nosource: Waiting for {0}, which is not installed. The rule stays here and runs again when it is back.
instinct.state.notarget: {0} is not installed, so there is nobody to ask. The rule stays here and runs again when it is back.
log.empty: Nothing to show. Either nothing has been said yet, or the filters and the levels on the right hide all of it.
log.sources.hint: How much of each one to show here and in the pane. The file under %APPDATA% keeps everything regardless.
log.title: What Meows and the plugins said
palette.hint: Type a plugin, a setting, something an open plugin is showing, or a line from the history. > for commands.
palette.strip.reset: Put every tab back where its plugin says
plugins.empty: Nothing found. Each plugin lives in its own subfolder of the plugins directory shown at the bottom of the window.
plugins.install.done: {0} is installed. It runs with the same rights as Meows, so switch it on only if you trust where it came from.
plugins.install.hint: A plugin from outside is a zip of its build folder: pick it with Install plugin…, or drop it on this tab. It runs with the same rights as Meows; install only what you trust.
plugins.install.pending: {0} is already installed and in use. The new version is beside it and takes over when Meows next starts.
plugins.install.replaced: {0} is replaced with the new version.
plugins.missingfile: {0} is missing from this plugin's folder. If you ran Meows straight out of the zip, extract the whole thing to a folder first and run it from there.
plugins.subtitle: Activate a plugin to give it a tab. Deactivating closes the tab and releases it.
plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.uninstall.done: {0} is removed. Its settings are still in the Meows settings folder, in case it comes back.
plugins.unloadable: This plugin cannot be loaded by this version of Meows.
plugins.update.none: Nothing installed from outside, so nothing to check.
plugins.update.task: Checking installed plugins for new versions
reach.error.hostkey: The server answered with the key SHA256:{0}, not the trusted SHA256:{1}. If the server was reinstalled, test and trust it again; if not, something is in the way.
reach.error.key: The SSH key could not be read: {0}. A wrong passphrase reads the same way.
reach.error.path: “{0}” is not a place under the server's folder. It has to be relative, with no .. in it.
reach.error.size: {0} arrived at the wrong size, so it was not put in place.
reach.missing.address: Fill in the host, the user and the folder on the server.
reach.missing.folder: Pick the folder plugins should copy to.
reach.missing.key: Choose the SSH key to log in with.
reach.missing.none: No server is set, so nothing is copied anywhere.
reach.missing.trust: Test the server and trust its key before anything is copied.
reach.test.newkey: Logged in to {0}. Its key is SHA256:{1}. Compare that with the server (ssh-keygen -lf on its host key) and press Trust if it matches.
reach.test.readonly: {0} is there, but would not take a file: {1}
reach.test.sftp: Logged in to {0}, and {1} is there.
rules.enabled: On or off. A rule that is off is kept and does nothing.
rules.notargets: None of the plugins installed says it can be asked to do anything yet, so there is nothing to put on the “then” side.
rules.onehop: One hop only: whatever a plugin does because a rule asked never starts another rule, so nothing can set off a chain while nobody is looking.
rules.subtitle: When one plugin does something, ask another to act. Every rule that fires writes what it asked for and what came back to the History tab.
rules.title: Rules
settings.bundle.hint: Everything Meows remembers, as one zip: preferences, which plugins are on, the bot folder, the history, every plugin's settings and data. Not the secrets, which are sealed to this machine and this account, and not the log.
settings.bundle.imported: Imported {0} files, {1} left out. What was here before is in {2}. Restart Meows so everything reads it.
settings.bundle.note: Importing writes over what is here, after keeping a copy of it as before-import-<date>.zip beside the settings, which can itself be imported to go back. Restart Meows afterwards so every plugin reads what arrived. Secrets in a bundle are never written.
settings.history.hint: The History tab records what every plugin did. It never forgets a line on its own unless you say how long to keep them.
settings.history.note: Older lines are forgotten when Meows starts and once a day while it runs; Purr lists that under Meows. The facts a plugin keeps and the hashes anything has seen are never forgotten. The History tab can forget by hand at any age, for one plugin or all.
settings.language.following: Windows is being followed, which works out as {0}.
settings.language.hint: Applies to the shell and to every plugin that ships the language. Anything a plugin has not translated stays in English rather than disappearing.
settings.names.hint: Every plugin is named after the cat. Each one also says what it is in plain words, and this picks which is on the tabs and the cards. The paw in the bottom bar is the same switch.
settings.names.plain: Plain names: Duplicates, Disk usage, Sorting
settings.outside.balloon: As tray balloons, without buttons: a Windows notification could not be set up here.
settings.outside.balloon.portable: As tray balloons, without buttons: a portable Meows writes nothing into the Start menu, which a Windows notification needs.
settings.outside.none: Not on this system; everything stays in the window.
settings.outside.toast: As Windows notifications, with their buttons, while the window is not in front. A state that holds all week, like a drive filling, stays in the window.
settings.server.folder: A folder: a share, a mapped drive, anything Windows can already open
settings.server.hint: The machine past this one: where the bot and Foundry run. Plugins that can put something there, Familiar's kits for one, copy to it; nothing is copied until a plugin asks.
settings.server.key.kept: A key is kept, sealed to this Windows account. The file it came from was not touched.
settings.server.key.notakey: {0} does not look like a private key. Pick the one without .pub.
settings.server.key.unreadable: That key could not be read: {0}
settings.server.passphrase: Passphrase, if the key has one
settings.server.passphrase.kept: A passphrase is kept. Type to replace it.
settings.server.trusted.now: Trusted. Plugins can copy to the server now.
settings.server.untrusted: No server key is trusted yet. Test, compare what it shows with the server, then Trust.
settings.startup.blocked: Windows has switched this off in its own startup list. Turn it back on in the Task Manager's Startup tab, or untick and tick this to register it afresh.
settings.startup.elsewhere: The startup list points at a different copy of Meows: {0}. Tick this again to point it here instead.
settings.startup.enabled: Start Meows when I log in
settings.startup.failed: Could not change the startup list: {0}
settings.startup.hint: Adds Meows to the per-user startup list, which is one entry you can also see and switch off in the Task Manager's Startup tab. No admin rights and no scheduled task.
settings.startup.intray: Start in the tray, without opening the window
settings.startup.intray.hint: The window is one click on the tray icon away.
settings.startup.path: It will start whichever copy of Meows this is:
settings.startup.unavailable: Meows cannot tell where it is running from, so it cannot register itself.
settings.storage.hint: Settings, plugin data and the log all live here, never in the folder you unzipped. Deleting this folder resets Meows completely.
settings.storage.portable: Portable: a file called portable sits beside Meows.exe, so everything is kept in data\ beside it and nothing is written to this user's profile. Remove the file to go back to the profile at the next start.
settings.storage.portable.how: To keep everything beside Meows.exe instead, for a stick or a folder that moves, put an empty file called portable (or portable.txt) next to Meows.exe and start Meows again. Export first and import there if what is here should come along.
settings.subtitle: How the window looks and what language it reads in. Both take effect straight away and are remembered.
settings.tabsize.hint: How big the tabs and group chips along the top are drawn. Larger ones are easier to hit and take another row when the strip wraps.
settings.theme.hint: Following the system means Meows changes with Windows, including when Windows switches itself at sunset.
settings.title: Settings
settings.tray.close: Closing the window keeps Meows running in the tray
settings.tray.close.hint: Quit is in the tray icon's menu. Untick this and the close button quits, as it used to.
settings.tray.hint: Meows sits in the notification area. Everything that watches or waits, Collar's dates, Birdwatch's refresh, a scan you started, carries on while the window is hidden, and the icon shows a dot when there is something to read.
shell.names.tip: Feline names on, plain names off
shell.notifications.empty: Nothing to report. Standing conditions stay here until the plugin that raised them clears them.
shell.palette.tip: Ctrl+K. Ctrl+Shift+K searches the tab in front; Ctrl+1 to 9 pick a tab.
shell.popout.away: This tab is in a window of its own.
shell.tasks.empty: Nothing running. Plugins register watches, imports and scheduled scans here; they stop when the plugin is deactivated.
shell.tasks.title: Background tasks
shell.update.only: Nothing installed from outside; a newer Meows is on the releases page.
strip.tab.newgroup.name: Name it
strip.tab.reset: Put it back where its plugin says
